name: Islamic Republic of Iran
summary: The state created by the 1979 revolution that overthrew the Shah: a theocratic republic led by a Supreme Leader, with an elected president and parliament.

knownFor.label: Persian carpets
knownFor.note: Hand-knotted carpets, an ancient craft still exported worldwide.

knownFor.label: Iranian cinema
knownFor.note: Directors such as Abbas Kiarostami and Asghar Farhadi won top international prizes.

knownFor.label: Iran–Iraq War
knownFor.note: An eight-year war that killed hundreds of thousands.

location.value: South-west Asia, between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf; about 1.65 million km².

terrain.value: Mountainous in the west (Zagros and Alborz ranges); desert basins such as the Kavir and Lut in the east.

climate.value: Diverse: arid and semi-arid in most places, subtropical along the Caspian coast.

resources.value: About 10% of the world’s oil reserves and 15% of its gas reserves.

disasters.value: Frequent earthquakes, such as the devastating Bam earthquake of 2003.

urbanisation.value: Tehran is the capital, largest city and main economic centre.

disease.value: Heavy COVID-19 losses; air pollution in big cities.

migration.value: Home to an estimated four million Afghan migrants and refugees; a mass deportation was ordered in May 2025.

economicBase.value: A centrally planned economy with large state ownership, based on oil and gas; Iran makes three-quarters of the world’s handmade carpets.

tradeRoutes.value: Sanctions have limited trade with the West; trade with China, Iraq, the UAE and Turkey.

wealth.value: An upper-middle-income country hit hard by sanctions and inflation.

moneyAndTax.value: The rial, which has lost most of its value since 1979.

inequality.value: Large gaps between rich and poor; high youth unemployment.

governmentType.value: An Islamic republic: the Supreme Leader is head of state, and an elected president heads the government.

keyRulers.value: Ruhollah Khomeini (Supreme Leader 1979–89). Ali Khamenei (Supreme Leader 1989–2026). Presidents such as Mohammad Khatami and Hassan Rouhani.

succession.value: The Assembly of Experts elects the Supreme Leader; presidents are elected for four years, but candidates must be approved by the Guardian Council.

institutions.value: The 12-member Guardian Council, the Assembly of Experts and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

stability.value: Protests after the disputed 2009 election, in 2019–20, in 2022 after Mahsa Amini died in police custody, and the largest protests since 1979 in 2025.

eliteConflict.value: Reformist presidents such as Khatami and Rouhani alternated with conservatives and hardliners.

armyAndTech.value: Regular army and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps; missiles and drones.

majorWars.value: Iran–Iraq War (1980–88); the Twelve-Day War with Israel (2025) and war with the US and Israel (2026); support for allied groups in Lebanon, Iraq and Yemen.

alliancesRivals.value: Rival of the US, Israel and Saudi Arabia; ties with Russia and China.

inventions.value: One of the world’s most scrutinised nuclear programmes; ballistic missiles and drones.

scienceEducation.value: High literacy; more than half of university students are women.

openness.value: Strict internet censorship, with social media and other sites blocked.

communicationTransport.value: Tehran Metro (1999); highways and railways across the plateau.

religion.value: Twelver Shia Islam is the state religion (90–95% of people); the Baháʼí Faith is not recognised and faces official persecution.

languageWriting.value: Persian (Farsi); Azeri, Kurdish, Arabic, Balochi and other languages.

artsArchitecture.value: Famous poets such as Rumi, Ferdowsi and Hafez; carpet weaving.

socialStructure.value: Persians are the largest group, followed by Azerbaijanis, with Kurds, Lurs, Arabs, Balochis and others.

sharedIdentity.value: A strong Persian identity linked to Shia Islam and ancient history.

dailyLife.value: City apartments and village houses; rice with stews (khoresh), bread and tea.

neighbours.value: Iraq, Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan.

ideasReligions.value: Spread its revolutionary ideas to Shia groups in the region.

colonisation.value: The Anglo-American coup of 1953 followed attempts to nationalise the oil industry.

peakPeriod.value: Influence in the region grew after 2003.

declineSignals.value: Western sanctions, high inflation and the largest protests since 1979 (2025).

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are documented; election fairness and protest death tolls are disputed.
